Position Summary

Manager – Semiconductor Operations, Risk & Transformation
Our Deloitte Regulatory, Risk & Forensic team helps client leaders translate multifaceted risk and an evolving regulatory environment into defensible actions that strengthen, protect, and transform their organization. Join our team and use advanced data, AI, and emerging technologies with industry insights to help clients bring clarity from complexity and accelerate their path to value creation.
Work you’ll do
As a Manager within Deloitte's Enterprise Operations & Risk (EO&R) practice, you will help semiconductor and technology clients address complex operational, strategic, and risk-related challenges. You will work closely with client leadership teams and Deloitte practitioners to design and deliver solutions that improve business performance, strengthen resilience, enable growth, and support large-scale transformation initiatives.
The role combines industry knowledge, problem solving, and client leadership across areas such as supply chain resilience, operational excellence, product quality, risk management, technology-enabled transformation, and business strategy. You will be responsible for managing client engagements, developing trusted stakeholder relationships, leading teams, and contributing to the growth of Deloitte's semiconductor sector capabilities.

- Lead and deliver client engagements focused on operations, risk, resilience, and transformation across semiconductor and technology organizations.

- Advise clients on complex business challenges related to manufacturing operations, supply chain performance, product quality, operational risk, workforce effectiveness, technology enablement, and organizational transformation.

- Support clients in identifying, assessing, and addressing risks across business operations, supply chains, third-party relationships, critical processes, and emerging technologies.

- Assist clients in designing and implementing operating models, governance frameworks, performance management approaches, risk management capabilities, and business process improvements.

- Support large-scale business and technology transformation initiatives, working across functions including operations, engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, technology, strategy, and risk.

- Structure complex business problems, conduct analyses, and develop practical recommendations that help clients achieve strategic and operational objectives.

- Build and maintain trusted relationships with client stakeholders and serve as a day-to-day advisor throughout the engagement lifecycle.

- Manage engagement planning, execution, budgets, staffing, reporting, and overall project delivery to ensure high-quality outcomes.

- Lead, coach, and develop engagement teams through effective delegation, mentoring, feedback, and performance management.

- Support business development activities including account planning, opportunity identification, proposal development, and pursuit support.

- Contribute to the development of Deloitte's semiconductor-focused offerings, thought leadership, and market eminence activities.

The successful candidate would possess these skills

- Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team

- Effective written and verbal communication skills

- Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product

- Ability to build and sustain professional relationships

- Ability to lead projects or workstreams

- Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment

- Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor

- Ability to meet deadlines

- Ability to mentor and provide clear guidance to others

The Team
Our Enterprise Operations & Risk offering enables clients to achieve profitable growth and competitive advantage by optimizing “heart of the business” operations. We leverage deep domain expertise to extend enterprise resilience, agility and remediation. Our professionals address client needs which span the organization and impact strategy, operations, performance and reputation.
Qualifications
Required

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, Economics, Technology, Public Policy, or a related field.

- 6–8 years of relevant experience in consulting, semiconductor, technology, manufacturing, industrial products, government, or related industries.

- Understanding of semiconductor industry dynamics, manufacturing operations, supply chain ecosystems, technology organizations, or related business environments.

- Experience supporting operational improvement, risk management, resilience, compliance, transformation, or strategic initiatives.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to assess complex business challenges and develop practical solutions.

- Experience managing projects, workstreams, and cross-functional teams.

- Strong executive communication, presentation, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills.

- Experience developing client deliverables, executive presentations, business cases, and strategic recommendations.

- Knowledge of emerging trends affecting the semiconductor and technology sectors, including supply chain resilience, workforce challenges, digital transformation, AI adoption, and evolving regulatory environments.

- Strong relationship-building and stakeholder management skills.

- Demonstrated leadership capability and experience developing high-performing teams.

- Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to identify opportunities and contribute to practice growth.

- Strong business and commercial acumen.

- Collaborative approach with the ability to work effectively across diverse teams and disciplines.

- Ability to travel 30-50%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.

- Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred

- Advanced degree and/or relevant professional certifications.

- Experience supporting semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, electronics, or technology-sector organizations .

- Experience with services associated to government affairs and navigating the ecosystem.

- Adaptability and comfort operating in ambiguous and evolving environments.

- Executive presence and confidence interacting with senior client leaders.

Industry Solution Leader - Oil, Gas & Chemical (Refining / Chemical Asset Performance)
Houston, Texas, United States · Forward Deployed Engineering · Employment Type: Full-Time
C3 AI (NYSE: AI), is the Enterprise AI application software company. C3 AI delivers a family of fully integrated products including the C3 Agentic AI Platform, an end-to-end platform for developing, deploying, and operating enterprise AI applications, C3 AI applications, a portfolio of industry-specific SaaS enterprise AI applications that enable the digital transformation of organizations globally, and C3 Generative AI, a suite of domain-specific generative AI offerings for the enterprise. Learn more at: C3 AI

C3 AI is seeking an Industry Solution Leader (ISL) for Oil, Gas & Chemical to lead the design and delivery of enterprise AI solutions for its clients with a specialization in Refining / Chemical Asset Performance.

Industry Solution Leaders combine deep industry and engineering expertise with end-to-end ownership of customer solutions. They are expected to understand a customer's operations deeply enough to challenge assumptions, identify and quantify the highest-value opportunities, define the right technical solution, and lead cross-functional teams through design, deployment, validation, and scale.

The role combines the responsibilities of a senior domain expert and solution leader. Industry Solution Leaders work directly with customer engineering, operations, maintenance, and executive teams while leading C3 AI Forward Deployed Engineers, data scientists, product teams, and other technical resources to deliver measurable business outcomes.

The ideal candidate brings significant hands-on experience in engineering, manufacturing, operations, reliability, or maintenance and has the technical judgment, customer leadership, and delivery ownership required to lead complex enterprise AI solutions from problem definition through production.

The ISL, Oil, Gas & Chemical - Refining / Chemical Asset Performance should have hands-on experience working inside a refinery, chemical plant, or similar continuous-process facility, including distillation, reactors, furnaces, compressors, heat exchangers, or utilities, with ownership of throughput, yield, energy, APC/process control, or reliability outcomes.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Own the overall solution strategy, technical direction, and delivery outcomes for assigned customer engagements, maintaining accountability from initial problem definition through production deployment and scale.

- Serve as the primary customer-facing solution leader and domain expert, developing a detailed understanding of customer operations, equipment, processes, constraints, and business objectives.

- Identify and quantify high-impact business opportunities across equipment reliability, maintenance, production performance, process optimization, throughput, yield, quality, energy efficiency, and operating economics.

- Translate complex engineering and operational challenges into tractable AI, machine learning, optimization, and software problems with clearly defined requirements, success criteria, and expected business value.

- Lead engagements through use case definition, requirements gathering, solution architecture, application configuration, validation, production deployment, user adoption, and scale-out.

- Apply deep engineering and industry expertise to challenge assumptions, evaluate technical approaches, interpret analytical results, and ensure solutions are consistent with engineering fundamentals and operational realities.

- Lead cross-functional teams of Forward Deployed Engineers, data scientists, product managers, engineers, and industry experts, establishing technical priorities and driving alignment around customer outcomes.

- Work directly with customer engineers, operators, reliability teams, maintenance organizations, and executives to validate requirements, solution performance, operational workflows, and business impact.

- Guide the interpretation and use of industrial data, including process signals, equipment attributes, operating states, maintenance history, production information, alarms, quality data, and other engineering information required to solve customer problems.

- Maintain accountability for solution quality, business value, technical risks, delivery progress, customer adoption, and executive communication throughout the engagement.

- Partner with C3 AI product management and engineering teams to identify reusable capabilities, inform product development, and scale successful solutions across assets, production lines, facilities, and business units.

- Support sales teams during opportunity assessment and capture by helping define customer problems, solution approaches, business value, technical requirements, deployment strategy, and demonstrations.

- Support development of statements of work and deployment plans, ensuring scope, deliverables, assumptions, data requirements, risks, timelines, and resource requirements are clearly defined.

- Develop repeatable industry methodologies, solution patterns, and best practices and represent C3 AI in relevant customer, industry, and technical forums.

QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline. Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Industrial, Mining, Metallurgical, Petroleum, Materials, or similar engineering backgrounds are preferred.

- 7+ years of experience in engineering, manufacturing, operations, reliability, maintenance, industrial technology, or technically focused consulting.

- Deep experience in one or more asset-intensive industries, including high-tech or semiconductor manufacturing, steel and metals, minerals and mining, utilities and power generation, oil and gas, chemicals, petrochemicals, LNG, pharmaceuticals, or heavy manufacturing.

- Demonstrated experience solving complex operational problems and improving equipment reliability, production performance, throughput, yield, quality, maintenance effectiveness, energy efficiency, or operating economics.

- Strong understanding of industrial equipment, manufacturing or production processes, process controls, maintenance practices, and operational workflows.

- Experience working with industrial data including sensor and time-series data, equipment states, alarms, maintenance history, production data, laboratory or quality information, equipment hierarchies, and engineering data.

- Experience with industrial systems such as process historians, SCADA, DCS, MES, EAM/CMMS, ERP, advanced process control, or industrial analytics platforms.

- Demonstrated ability to reason from engineering fundamentals and determine whether analytical and AI-driven recommendations are physically, technically, and operationally credible.

- Demonstrated experience leading complex, customer-facing technical engagements and working directly with engineering, operational, and executive stakeholders.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to structure ambiguous problems, establish priorities, and drive teams toward practical solutions.

- Ability to work effectively with software engineers, data scientists, product managers, and customer technical teams and translate between domain, business, and technical requirements.

- Excellent presentation, written communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills.

- Ability to travel to customer locations as required.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience delivering AI, machine learning, advanced analytics, optimization, predictive maintenance, condition monitoring, process optimization, or industrial digital transformation solutions.

- Hands-on technical experience working with industrial data, SQL, Python, analytics tools, application configuration, scripting, or similar technologies, with the ability to directly inspect data, prototype analyses, and troubleshoot solution behavior.

- Experience with rotating equipment, electrical equipment, production equipment, manufacturing lines, process units, mining systems, utility assets, or other complex industrial systems.

- Experience taking technical solutions from initial proof of value through production deployment and scale.

- Experience scaling solutions across multiple assets, plants, facilities, or business units.

- Advanced degree in Engineering, Science, or a related technical discipline.

This leader sets the vision for service differentiation, aligns cross-functional teams, and builds scalable service products and capabilities to improve customer outcomes. This highly complex role acts as an interface between Go-to-Market teams, Business Units (BUs), and Engineering teams, driving service solutions, ensuring roadmap alignment to customer High‑Value Problems (HVPs), and delivering measurable business results across regions and various market segments.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic & Organizational Leadership

- Lead senior managers, ensuring alignment to business objectives and execution plans based on portfolio focuses for CVD/DDP products

- Enable the team to identify gaps to plans across the field and develop corrective actions to ensure delivery against business goals.

- Orchestrate and articulate functional and cross‑functional plan that support BU priorities and customer engagement.

- Oversee organizational and personnel decisions to ensure efficient operations and scalable execution in SBU.

- Shape critical strategic review process and includes plans to address strategic issue for 5-year horizon.

Engineering & Program Leadership

- Guide engineering organizations responsible for the design, development, and implementation of service programs.

- Lead strategy and content development for Product Review meetings.

- Ensure programs are delivered in accordance with approved budgets, schedules, and quality expectations. Accountable for the ownership to drive related service revenue growth and margin improvement initiatives.

- Anticipate future technical needs and drive the development of innovative engineering approaches aligned to SBU product strategy.

- Direct the teams in resolving complex engineering and product issues through direct engagement with internal and external customers.

- Develop and implement approval path to advance service product advancement.

Cross‑Functional Execution

- Be accountable for product performance and results on the region or account segment basis.

- Enable cross-functional execution across stakeholders to operationalize direction and deliver intended business outcomes.

- Partner with senior AGS business and BU leaders to ensure initiatives address high‑value business problems and align with organizational direction.

Product Portfolio & Business Strategy

- Lead development of integrated product and portfolio plan in partnership with BUs, aligning long‑range roadmap, engineering specifications, and business goals to drive market success.

- Partner with leaders in CVD/DDP Business Units, Sales/Marketing teams, and Field teams to execute market‑focused product strategies.

- Based on market segmentations, guide the team to identify priority segments, and determine where to actively invest and compete.

Market, Customer & Competitive Insight

- Lead with deep, expert‑level understanding of global market, technical, and competitive trends across segments.

- Oversee a systematic process based on competitive intelligence to inform priorities and execution.

- Direct the team to map market trends, opportunities, and threats to product roadmaps and functional direction.

- Guide the team to understand customer roadmaps and High‑Value Problems, ensuring priorities are reflected in product and engineering plans.

- Contribute as a key member of competitive “red team” analysis and strategic customer engagements.

Field, Sales & Customer Engagement

- Provide strategic oversight and oversee customer escalation path across SBU and across regions.

- Serve with a leadership voice as an interface between Sales and Business Units to ensure field alignment and consistent messaging.

- Conduct executive‑level customer and field engagements, including calls with Field Technical Directors.

- Present periodic state‑of‑the‑business updates and performance reviews to BU and senior leadership.

- 15+ years of progressive experience across engineering, product management, business strategy, or related leadership roles.

- Strong combination of technical expertise and business/commercial judgment.

- Proven ability to develop and execute product, portfolio, or market strategies in complex environments.

- Strong communication and influence skills with experience engaging senior leaders, customers, and cross‑functional partners.

- Experience supporting global or multi‑regional business units.

Job Description Summary
GE Vernova’s Gas Power business engineers advanced, efficient natural gas-powered technologies and services, along with decarbonization solutions that help enable a lower-carbon future. In this role, you will be accountable for the full project lifecycle, from contract signing through completion of all contractual obligations. You will ensure customer satisfaction by effectively managing project activities, resources, timelines, and cross-functional teams, while driving successful delivery of customer equipment, facilities, or infrastructure projects.

This role also carries responsibility for project delivery, profit and loss performance, and adherence to budgets and operating plans. Working with moderate to high autonomy, you will use strong evaluative judgment and operational acumen to influence outcomes, improve ways of working, and support business objectives.

Key Responsibilities
Customer & Stakeholder Leadership

- Serve as first and primary customer contact for assigned projects

Project Execution & Governance

- Employ advanced operational, engineering, and product management techniques across interdependent workstreams

- Collaborate closely with partnering functions to resolve cross‑functional issues and execution constraints

Team Leadership & Matrix Management

- Support Functional Project Managers with escalations across functions, customers, and partners

- Present project, business, or technical solutions to internal and external senior leadership teams

- Influence without authority in a matrix organization to drive unified execution

- Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university

- Minimum 7 years of Project Management experience within Power Generation Equipment, Construction, or large capital project environments

- Flexibility to travel occasionally to customer sites and other locations to support project execution up to 30% of the time.

Desired Characteristics

- Experience and demonstrated understanding of large capital project execution costs and estimates.

- Certified Project Management Professional

- Field experience, Project Management, or equivalent experience.

- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple phased projects simultaneously and independently.

- Demonstrated strong customer focus and the ability to foster strong relationships; Experience working with and influencing senior level leaders. Demonstrated strategic thinking, problem solving, business and financial acumen.

- Strong oral and written communication skills. Demonstrated presentation skills and ability to succinctly communicate complex messages.

- An inclusive style and strong interpersonal and leaderships skills at all levels to gain acceptance and buy in from other matrix functions to accomplish goals.

- Demonstrated ability to make independent decisions, manage conflicting priorities in a fast-paced environment and effectively interface at all organizational levels

- Experience applying data and lean tools and technologies for strategic, operational and project efficiencies

Job Posting Title
Advanced ME Manager
Job Description Summary
Dauch is looking for an Advanced Manufacturing Engineering Manager to join our team in Newton, NC. This is a fully onsite role.

The Advanced ME Manager will provide first level day-to-day administrative and technical leadership for a staff of professional engineers and technicians within the manufacturing engineering and program launch department, to accomplish specific engineering projects. They are responsible for the results of the department's efforts and for the effectiveness of their overall integration with other departments.
Job Description:

- Benchmarks manufacturing processes with other Dauch sites and ensures that relevant plans are in place to close gaps.

- Manages and leads capex requirements for Newton, ensuring that local budgets are in line with divisional requirements. Plans and track capex spending and communicate status and phasing.

- Works with purchasing to ensure all equipment ordered (including spare parts) is compliant with divisional specifications and safety standards.

- Ensures that all systems relating to manufacturing engineering are up to date and appropriate for the business needs and Dauch requirements.

- Ensures core process compliancy for site’s key processes (ex. hardening, welding, assembly, etc.).

- Leads BPE (Business Process Excellence) projects to improve systems.

- Consolidates all OGS budgets and track each area for compliance and improvements.

- Provides a consolidated view of demand/capacity at plant level for the next five years, ensuring that actual vs target is clear and with relevant improvement activities.

- Compares customer data to iDash and manage any exceptions.

- Responds to MS Divisional requirements with regard to - Capacity analysis, investment/capex requirements and other ad hoc requests.

- Collaborates with Supply Chain and Commercial functions to ensure SIOP and MPS are carried out for Capacity Management.

- Leads the facilities maintenance team to adhere to plant needs and those that are aligned with industrialization.

- Leads implementation of industrial solutions to improve pp2.

- Supports NBA with process cost per part and investment and tooling cost requirements.

- Establish standard process and cycle times at SOP. Ensures process delivers target performance at SOP.

- Hands over MS deliverables at SOP; operator work instructions, PFMEA, stage-drawings, PPM etc.).

- Leads process-related CIMS projects

- Provides input into the VA/VE system.

- Supports problem solving activities.

- Actively encourages the participation of all engineers in identifying and realizing improvement opportunities.

- Manages engineering team and ensures work follows divisional process, procedure and standards.

- Develops a diverse and inclusive team aligned to GKN philosophy.

- Motivates team by setting challenging and achievable goals. Communicates business strategy and updates team on the roadmap to excellence.

- Creates a culture of Engagement where all associates have the tools they need to do their job well and have the opportunity to contribute to improvement through associate involvement.

- Leads plant level NVH activities to include vehicle correlation, rig test limits and monitoring.

- Ensures plant level ECU software related to assembly/test production meets Dauch and customer requirements.

- Ensures prototype parts are produced to support current and future programs.

- All other duties as assigned.

Required Skills and Education

- Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or other relevant field.

- 8+ years of experience in a Manufacturing Engineering Leadership role, preferably in the automotive industry.

- Experience with capex planning and tracking.

- Experience with APQP, PPAP, PFMEA, and control plans.

- Knowledge of automation, robotics, PLCs, and Industry 4.0 technologies.

- Willingness and ability to travel up to approximately 25%.

Dauch Corporation is a premier Driveline and Metal Forming supplier serving the global automotive industry with a powertrain-agnostic product portfolio that supports electric, hybrid, and internal combustion vehicles. The company is headquartered in Detroit, MI, with operations that span 24 countries and more than 175 locations. Formed through the acquisition of Dowlais Group plc and its subsidiaries - GKN Automotive and GKN Powder Metallurgy, Dauch unites deep engineering roots with global manufacturing capabilities and an entrepreneurial spirit to move mobility forward. Manager / Senior Manager, Technical Operations
San Diego, California, United States

ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with neffy® , the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you’re motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Manager / Sr. Manager, Technical Operations will play a key role in executing Technical Operations programs that support the continued development and commercial supply of neffy™. The successful candidate will combine strong technical judgment, project management, and external partner leadership in a highly collaborative environment.

Working closely with internal stakeholders and CMOs, this role provides technical and operational leadership across the ARS outsourced manufacturing network. Responsibilities include leading Technical Operations projects, supporting formulation and process development, technology transfer, GMP manufacturing activities, and resolution of technical and operational issues. The position ensures project scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, and budgets remain aligned while proactively identifying and escalating risks to support compliant, reliable, and on-time product supply.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Manage cross-functional Technical Operations projects and day-to-day technical and operational interactions with assigned external partners, including scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, budgets, risks, key milestones, project meetings, action tracking, scopes of work, proposals, change orders, and CMO/vendor performance metrics and KPIs (e.g., service, quality, delivery, capacity, and right-first-time).

- Serve as a Technical Operations point of contact for assigned external manufacturing partners and work closely with CMOs and internal stakeholders to ensure execution against agreed project plans and supply requirements.

- Provide technical oversight of formulation and process development, scale-up, technology transfer, process characterization, process validation/PPQ, and continued process verification activities, as applicable.

- Plan and support clinical and commercial manufacturing campaigns in coordination with CMOs, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and other internal functions; provide on-site/person-in-plant support for key manufacturing activities as needed.

- Review manufacturing and process documentation, including master and executed batch records, protocols, reports, process performance data, vendor change controls, investigations, and annual/product reviews, for technical accuracy and process performance.

- Lead or support technical assessment and resolution of manufacturing deviations, out-of-specification or atypical results, and other process issues; contribute to root-cause analysis and appropriate corrective and preventive actions in partnership with Quality Assurance.

- Assess proposed manufacturing and process changes for technical impact and support cross-functional evaluation of quality, supply, and regulatory implications.

- Monitor and trend manufacturing and process performance data to identify emerging risks, process drift, and opportunities for continuous improvement and operational excellence.

- Support vendor selection, onboarding, and qualification activities in collaboration with Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Procurement, and other stakeholders.

- Communicate project status, technical risks, manufacturing issues, and recommend actions clearly to Technical Operations leadership and cross-functional stakeholders; escalate significant issues to appropriate decision-makers.

- Support preparation and review of CMC information for regulatory submissions and responses to health authority questions, as required.

- Support Technical Operations process improvement, business continuity, capacity planning, and other strategic operational initiatives as assigned.

- Support commercial supply operations managed within Technical Operations, including coordination with third-party logistics (3PL) providers, distribution partners, and external manufacturing/packaging partners to maintain reliable product supply.

- Support product serialization activities, including EPCIS data exchange and operational compliance with applicable Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) requirements, working with packaging, distribution, Quality Assurance, and other partners as appropriate.

- Support clinical supply activities, including coordination with Clinical Operations and external vendors for clinical packaging, labeling, distribution, inventory/expiry management, and Interactive Response Technology/Interactive Web Response System (IRT/IWRS) activities, as applicable.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

- Strong working knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), pharmaceutical manufacturing operations, and applicable quality systems and regulatory expectations.

- Demonstrated technical understanding of formulation, manufacturing processes, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation, and process performance sufficient to critically evaluate CMO data and recommendations, work effectively in cross-functional technical teams, and hold external partners accountable to commitments.

- Strong project and vendor management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, timelines, deliverables, and external partners in a fast-paced environment.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate complex manufacturing or process issues, develop recommendations, and communicate the rationale for action.

- Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate effectively across functions and organizational levels, including senior management and external partners.

- Well-organized, detail-oriented, and able to identify and escalate risks while maintaining focus on execution and business priorities.

- Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project/reporting tools; experience with project management, continuous improvement, or operational excellence methodologies is a plus.

- Working knowledge of commercial and clinical supply operations relevant to Technical Operations, including 3PL interfaces, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA requirements, and clinical IRT/IWRS processes; direct experience in one or more of these areas is preferred.

- Must be able to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 20% to support external manufacturing partners and key project activities.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

- Bachelor’s degree in pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry, chemical engineering, engineering, or a related scientific/technical discipline; an advanced degree is a plus. An acceptable combination of education and relevant experience will also be considered.

- Minimum of 5 years of relevant pharmaceutical/biotechnology experience in Technical Operations, manufacturing, process/formulation development, CMC, supply chain, or a related function.

- Experience working with external CMOs/CDMOs and supporting GMP clinical and/or commercial manufacturing is strongly preferred.

- Experience with drug-device combination products, nasal/inhalation products, sterile manufacturing, commercial product launch, or PPQ is preferred.

- Experience reviewing manufacturing batch records and process documentation and supporting technical investigations, change controls, and regulatory CMC activities is preferred.

- Experience supporting commercial distribution/3PL operations, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA compliance, and/or clinical supply and IRT/IWRS activities is preferred.

Denver, CO
Hybrid

Quindar builds software to manage satellites like servers. We are seeking a Vice President of Operations to build the operating system, organizational infrastructure, and business processes that turn company strategy into execution as we scale across commercial and government markets.
This leader owns business operations, strategy and performance, facilities, and General & Administrative functions. Beyond running the operating cadence, the role connects corporate strategy, resource allocation, and cross-functional execution so that Quindar consistently makes the right investments and turns them into business outcomes. The role holds the authority to resolve cross-functional prioritization conflicts at the leadership level, with clear and intentional escalation to the CEO, while functional leaders retain accountability for their results and authority over their teams.
Facilities, Business Operations, and the G&A team report to this role, with their leaders responsible for day-to-day execution. This is a hands-on executive role for someone who can build a function, develop its leaders, and drive execution across the company.

Company Execution and Performance Management
• Translate company strategy into company OKRs and functional commitments with accountable owners, deadlines, dependencies, and approved resources.
• Agree with each functional leader on a small set of meaningful KPIs with clear definitions, source data, targets, and reporting frequency, and maintain a consolidated performance dashboard across Sales, Product, Engineering, Programs, Finance, People and Brand, and Operations.
• Design and run the company operating model: quarterly planning, leadership reviews, decision tracking, and follow-up, with a visible record of commitments delivered, missed, corrected, and rescoped.
• Design and implement a company-wide model for cross-functional prioritization and decision-making at the leadership level, including decision rights and escalation paths, aligned with and actively reinforced by the CEO.
• Use the operating data to drive decisions and corrective actions, resolve cross-functional dependencies, and escalate decisions that put company goals at risk.
• Partner with functional leaders and the VP of Finance to align workforce capacity, hiring plans, facilities, and budgets with company priorities.

Corporate Strategy and Go-to-Market

AI-Enabled Business Operations

• Identify and baseline the highest-value workflows across functions, prioritizing those that remove coordination overhead between Product, Engineering, Programs, Sales, and Marketing (for example, specifications to engineering tickets, user documentation, marketing materials, and proposal development).
• Build internal knowledge infrastructure, such as a company data warehouse of product knowledge, engineering designs, documentation, and marketing and proposal content, that any role can query or use to create collateral through an agentic interface.
• Implement appropriate access controls, source traceability, and compliance requirements, including CUI handling, before any workflow handling sensitive or consequential outputs enters production use.

Facilities and Classified Readiness

General and Administrative Operations
• Lead legal operations, and corporate administrative services through internal teams and outside partners.
• Manage outside counsel and coordinate corporate legal matters, employment matters, contract review, and company policies.
• Own cap table and stock option administration in partnership with Finance and legal counsel, and maintain corporate records and board and stockholder approval workflows with the CEO and counsel.
• Own the administrative infrastructure required to pursue and support government business, including SAM.gov registration, applicable NSTXL and consortium memberships, JCP certification/DD Form 2345, and a centralized calendar of registrations, renewals, and reporting obligations.
• Oversee export compliance program administration, including applicable ITAR/EAR processes, working with qualified counsel and designated compliance personnel.
• Coordinate corporate insurance, business continuity planning, corporate overhead efficiency, and company-wide operational risk management.

Fundraising and Finance Partnership
• Lead operational, legal, people, and corporate diligence readiness for fundraising alongside the VP of Finance, including an organized data room and timely, accurate responses to investor requests.
• Support board materials and investor reporting with company operating metrics, organizational plans, and progress against strategic priorities.
• Partner with Finance on operating plans, overhead budgets, and the investments needed to support the next stage of growth and new business lines.

• Experience leading operations at a growing technology company, with exposure to government contracting or another regulated market.
• Demonstrated success building teams, systems, and operating processes through a significant stage of organizational growth.
• Experience contributing to corporate strategy and leading cross-functional GTM or new-business initiatives from concept to launch, with a bias toward revenue and business outcomes.
• Experience across facilities, legal operations, compliance, or business operations.
• A hands-on track record of using AI, technology, and automation to improve operational efficiency.
• Familiarity with venture-backed company governance, equity administration, and fundraising diligence.
• Ability to turn ambiguous priorities into clear plans, coordinate executive peers, and hold teams accountable for commitments.
• Strong judgment about when to act directly, delegate, escalate, or engage specialist expertise.

• Cross-functional prioritization decisions are made quickly and consistently at the leadership level, with less day-to-day intervention from the CEO.

• AI-enabled workflows are in production across functions, materially reducing manual coordination while meeting access-control and compliance requirements.

Manager / Senior Manager, Technical Operations
San Diego, California, United States

ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with neffy® , the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you’re motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Manager / Sr. Manager, Technical Operations will play a key role in executing Technical Operations programs that support the continued development and commercial supply of neffy™. The successful candidate will combine strong technical judgment, project management, and external partner leadership in a highly collaborative environment.

Working closely with internal stakeholders and CMOs, this role provides technical and operational leadership across the ARS outsourced manufacturing network. Responsibilities include leading Technical Operations projects, supporting formulation and process development, technology transfer, GMP manufacturing activities, and resolution of technical and operational issues. The position ensures project scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, and budgets remain aligned while proactively identifying and escalating risks to support compliant, reliable, and on-time product supply.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Manage cross-functional Technical Operations projects and day-to-day technical and operational interactions with assigned external partners, including scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, budgets, risks, key milestones, project meetings, action tracking, scopes of work, proposals, change orders, and CMO/vendor performance metrics and KPIs (e.g., service, quality, delivery, capacity, and right-first-time).

- Serve as a Technical Operations point of contact for assigned external manufacturing partners and work closely with CMOs and internal stakeholders to ensure execution against agreed project plans and supply requirements.

- Provide technical oversight of formulation and process development, scale-up, technology transfer, process characterization, process validation/PPQ, and continued process verification activities, as applicable.

- Plan and support clinical and commercial manufacturing campaigns in coordination with CMOs, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and other internal functions; provide on-site/person-in-plant support for key manufacturing activities as needed.

- Review manufacturing and process documentation, including master and executed batch records, protocols, reports, process performance data, vendor change controls, investigations, and annual/product reviews, for technical accuracy and process performance.

- Lead or support technical assessment and resolution of manufacturing deviations, out-of-specification or atypical results, and other process issues; contribute to root-cause analysis and appropriate corrective and preventive actions in partnership with Quality Assurance.

- Assess proposed manufacturing and process changes for technical impact and support cross-functional evaluation of quality, supply, and regulatory implications.

- Monitor and trend manufacturing and process performance data to identify emerging risks, process drift, and opportunities for continuous improvement and operational excellence.

- Support vendor selection, onboarding, and qualification activities in collaboration with Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Procurement, and other stakeholders.

- Communicate project status, technical risks, manufacturing issues, and recommend actions clearly to Technical Operations leadership and cross-functional stakeholders; escalate significant issues to appropriate decision-makers.

- Support preparation and review of CMC information for regulatory submissions and responses to health authority questions, as required.

- Support Technical Operations process improvement, business continuity, capacity planning, and other strategic operational initiatives as assigned.

- Support commercial supply operations managed within Technical Operations, including coordination with third-party logistics (3PL) providers, distribution partners, and external manufacturing/packaging partners to maintain reliable product supply.

- Support product serialization activities, including EPCIS data exchange and operational compliance with applicable Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) requirements, working with packaging, distribution, Quality Assurance, and other partners as appropriate.

- Support clinical supply activities, including coordination with Clinical Operations and external vendors for clinical packaging, labeling, distribution, inventory/expiry management, and Interactive Response Technology/Interactive Web Response System (IRT/IWRS) activities, as applicable.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

- Strong working knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), pharmaceutical manufacturing operations, and applicable quality systems and regulatory expectations.

- Demonstrated technical understanding of formulation, manufacturing processes, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation, and process performance sufficient to critically evaluate CMO data and recommendations, work effectively in cross-functional technical teams, and hold external partners accountable to commitments.

- Strong project and vendor management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, timelines, deliverables, and external partners in a fast-paced environment.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate complex manufacturing or process issues, develop recommendations, and communicate the rationale for action.

- Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate effectively across functions and organizational levels, including senior management and external partners.

- Well-organized, detail-oriented, and able to identify and escalate risks while maintaining focus on execution and business priorities.

- Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project/reporting tools; experience with project management, continuous improvement, or operational excellence methodologies is a plus.

- Working knowledge of commercial and clinical supply operations relevant to Technical Operations, including 3PL interfaces, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA requirements, and clinical IRT/IWRS processes; direct experience in one or more of these areas is preferred.

- Must be able to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 20% to support external manufacturing partners and key project activities.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

- Bachelor’s degree in pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry, chemical engineering, engineering, or a related scientific/technical discipline; an advanced degree is a plus. An acceptable combination of education and relevant experience will also be considered.

- Minimum of 5 years of relevant pharmaceutical/biotechnology experience in Technical Operations, manufacturing, process/formulation development, CMC, supply chain, or a related function.

- Experience working with external CMOs/CDMOs and supporting GMP clinical and/or commercial manufacturing is strongly preferred.

- Experience with drug-device combination products, nasal/inhalation products, sterile manufacturing, commercial product launch, or PPQ is preferred.

- Experience reviewing manufacturing batch records and process documentation and supporting technical investigations, change controls, and regulatory CMC activities is preferred.

- Experience supporting commercial distribution/3PL operations, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA compliance, and/or clinical supply and IRT/IWRS activities is preferred.

Actual pay rates are determined by considering multiple factors including qualifications, relevance of experience, education & credentials, subject matter expertise, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

This position is also eligible for Equity, 401k matching, and our excellent benefits package including 100% employer paid Medical, Dental & Vision for employees. View the full package here: ARS Careers Page

Manager / Senior Manager, Quality Assurance
San Diego, California, United States

ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with neffy® , the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you’re motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture.

This is a hands-on role that will work an onsite hybrid schedule at our San Diego corporate office in the Carmel Valley area. The Manager / Senior Manager Quality Assurance owns batch disposition and product complaint management for products made at our contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs). You will review executed batch records, drive deviations and investigations to closure, and run the complaint process end to end so that every lot released meets cGMP and regulatory requirements. This is a hands-on role working daily with CMO quality teams, Regulatory, Supply Chain, and Medical Affairs.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Batch record review and disposition

- Review executed batch records, packaging records, and certificates of analysis from CMOs for accuracy, completeness, and cGMP compliance.

- Verify that deviations, OOS/OOT results, and change controls tied to each lot are closed or properly assessed before release.

- Prepare lot disposition packages and recommend release, rejection, or quarantine; act as QA approver per delegation.

- Review master batch records and specifications for new and revised products.

- Track batch release timelines and partner with Supply Chain to meet commercial and clinical supply needs.

Product complaint management

- Own the product complaint process: intake, triage, CMO investigation requests, trending, and closure within defined timelines.

- Assess complaints for reportability (e.g., Field Alert Reports, MDRs for combination products) with Regulatory and Pharmacovigilance.

- Lead or support root cause investigations and confirm CAPAs are effective.

- Prepare complaint trend reports for management review and Annual Product Reviews.

CMO Quality Oversight

- Serve as day-to-day QA contact for assigned CMOs and testing labs.

- Review and approve CMO deviations, investigations, change controls, and CAPAs affecting our products.

- Manage quality agreements and quality metrics; join business reviews and person-in-plant visits as needed.

- Support CMO audits and regulatory inspections.

GMP compliance and quality systems

- Maintain compliance with 21 CFR Parts 210/211, 21 CFR Part 4 (combination products), ICH Q7–Q10, and EU GMP as applicable.

- Author and revise SOPs for batch disposition and complaint handling.

- Contribute to Annual Product Reviews, recall readiness, and inspection readiness.

- Lead process improvements, and represent QA on cross-functional project teams.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

- Quality judgment: makes sound, documented release and reportability decisions under time pressure.

- Partner management: holds CMOs to standards while keeping relationships productive.

- Communication: writes clear investigation summaries and explains risk to non-QA colleagues.

- Ownership: tracks open items to closure without being chased.

- Primarily office-based work with occasional travel to CMO sites, including time in GMP manufacturing areas with gowning. Occasional after-hours support for urgent complaints or release needs.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Required

- Preferred Bachelor's degree in chemistry, biology, pharmacy, engineering, or related science. An acceptable combination of education and relevant experience will also be considered

- Minimum of 6+ years of QA experience

- Hands-on batch record review and lot disposition for commercial pharmaceutical or combination products.

- Direct experience managing product complaints, deviations, and CAPAs.

- Working knowledge of cGMP (21 CFR 210/211), ICH guidelines, and FDA expectations.

- Experience overseeing CMOs or external testing labs in a virtual or outsourced model.

- Strong technical writing and attention to detail.

Preferred

- Drug-device combination product experience (21 CFR Part 4, 820 / QMSR).

- Sterile, nasal, or inhalation dosage form experience.

- Electronic QMS experience (e.g., Veeva Vault QualityDocs/QMS, MasterControl).

- ASQ certification (CQA, CQE, or CPGP).

At ARS, we are proud to offer a highly competitive compensation & benefits package.

The full-time salary range for this posted position is $145,000 to $185,000 and may be eligible for a discretionary annual performance bonus. Actual pay rates are determined by considering multiple factors including qualifications, relevance of experience, education & credentials, subject matter expertise, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

This position is also eligible for Equity, 401k matching, and our excellent benefits package including 100% employer paid Medical, Dental & Vision for employees. View the full package here: ARS Careers Page

If you are interested in applying for an employment opportunity and require special assistance or an accommodation to apply due to a disability, please contact us at careers@ars-pharma.com

Director, Facility Operations
The 3-time WNBA Champions Los Angeles Sparks are seeking an innovative, strategic, and revenue-driven Director, Facility Operations . This executive will be responsible for working with both in-house employees and 3rd party vendors, and will oversee the day-to-day upkeep and operation of the Los Angeles Sparks’ Training Facility.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

- Oversee the operation of building systems and equipment, including mechanical, electrical, plumbing, hydro, and food service equipment and direct the work of personnel associated with the systems and building engineering.

- Serve at the primary point of contact for building maintenance, repairs, and facilities-related service requests across all organizational spaces, including offices and venues.

- Assist in the development and implementation of a computerized work order management system to enable occupants to submit service requests, track progress, and support the prioritization and scheduling of maintenance and repair activities.

- Serve as point of contact for local utilities (ex. Southern California Edison for building power).

- Serve as the primary building point of contact for the Fire Marshal, coordinate and attend required inspections, maintain all necessary fire and life safety records and documentation, and schedule and oversee required annual, quarterly, and other periodic testing of building safety systems in accordance with applicable codes and jurisdictional requirements.

- Build and maintain budgets for annual preventative maintenance costs.

- Develop and maintain appropriate inventory levels of supplies, materials, and repair parts based on facility and venue needs, ensuring materials are readily available to support maintenance and repair activities, and maintain accurate inventory records.

- Develop and oversee annual and preventive maintenance schedules for all facilities and building systems; establish and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs) for facility operations, maintenance, and emergency response; and identify, engage, and manage third-party vendors to support venue operations, including establishing clear emergency response protocols and service expectation.

- Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, supply usage, labor, and associated costs to track facility performance, identify maintenance trends, and inform the development of a long-term asset management and replacement program Develop service contract requirements, scope of work, performance standards, and service-level expectations for third-party vendors to ensure facility maintenance and operational needs are clearly defined and consistently met.

- Oversee and direct housekeeping services and cleaning services for back of house spaces, player spaces, and office spaces.

- Demonstrate knowledge of professional sports hardwood court cleaning practices and maintenance requirements to ensure the playing surface meets the standards and operational needs of a professional sports team.

- Oversee and coordinate specialty window cleaning and other specialized cleaning services, ensuring work is performed safely, effectively, and in accordance with facility standards.

- Build and maintain strong working relationships with team personnel to understand facility-related needs and requests, coordinate service delivery, and ensure clear, timely, and consistent communication.

- Working alongside Food Service team and associated personnel, coordinate repairs to equipment essential to food and beverage operations as needed.

- Working alongside team trainers, schedule servicing hydrotherapy equipment as required.

- Oversee and direct the work of landscaping team to ensure trees and plants (indoor and outdoor) are maintained.

- Collect and maintain accurate records to track venue assets, with an ability to identify faulty equipment, or make recommendations based on anticipated lifecycle for asset replacement.

- Track warranties of building assets.

- Conduct frequent physical inspections of building and external grounds to ensure the highest industry standards are met in Maintenance, System Operations, identifying and communicating any potential safety concerns, and areas requiring follow-up attention.

- Other duties, as assigned, related to the upkeep, maintenance and operation of the Sparks’ Training Facility.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

- Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in facility maintenance, building systems management, and facilities oversight, including supervisory or managerial responsibilities. Experience in a professional sports or large-scale venue environment is strongly preferred.

- Demonstrated knowledge of building systems and facility maintenance, including HVAC systems (air- and water-cooled systems, humidity control, and ventilation), fire and life safety systems, electrical systems, plumbing, and exterior grounds maintenance. Ability to oversee preventive maintenance, troubleshoot facility issues, and coordinate specialized contractors to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient building operations.

- Experience leading maintenance personnel and managing third-party service providers, with the ability to establish maintenance standards, oversee service delivery, and ensure facilities meet the operational requirements of a professional sports organization.

- Understanding of basketball schedules and basic team operations.

- Ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects simultaneously, working efficiently, to meet deadlines, with an excellent eye for detail.

- Strong interpersonal, organizational, computer and communication skills, as well as analytical skills.

- A proven ability to think critically and set priorities.

- Innovative thinker with success in developing and implementing new ideas and programs.

- Ability to anticipate and resolve problems and conflicts.

- Available to respond to emergencies 24/7.

- Ability to maintain a high level of Professionalism in all circumstances.

- Ability to work frequent irregular and long hours, weekends, evenings and all full-stadium events through completion and departure of public and team personnel as appropriate.

Compensation commensurate with experience; minimum starting salary at $105,000 annually.
